data.name: Sharanshak
data.gender_notes: Sharanshak is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Sharanshak is derived from the Sanskrit words Shara (protection) and Ansh (path). It means the protector of the path, one who guides and shields on the journey of life. The name Sharanshak carries the meaning “Protector of Path” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharanshak usually hope their child will grow to embody protector of path and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sharanshak is a name that signifies the divine presence of a guardian angel or a trusted spiritual guide who is always there to protect and guide us on our life's journey.
data.etymology: Sharanshak belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector of Path.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharanshak total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Sharanshak is derived from the Sanskrit words "Shara" meaning chariot and "Anshak" meaning protector. This name symbolizes one who rides the chariot of life, seeking protection and guidance from the divine, to navigate through the journey of existence. It represents a devotee whose faith is unwavering, and who seeks shelter and support from the higher power, to overcome the challenges of life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sharanshak was a king of the Shaka Empire in ancient India, ruling from around 120 BC to 100 BC. The name Sharanshak carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Sharanshak was a prominent ruler of the Shaka Empire, which originated in modern-day Sindh, Pakistan, and spread to parts of present-day Gujarat, India.
